references.text: The same principle that an animal must stay with its mother for a certain period before it can be used, here in the context that the animal shall not be slaughtered before the eighth day.
Circumcision on the eighth day parallels the requirement that animals may first be offered from the eighth day.
A similar principle of a waiting period before something can be used for holy purposes, here regarding fruit trees.
Continuation of the rules about offering animals, where a cow or sheep shall not be slaughtered on the same day as its offspring.
The firstborn of cattle and small livestock are to be given to the Lord, and they must stay with their mother for seven days before they can be offered.
The firstborn of cattle, sheep, and goats shall not be redeemed but offered as a fire offering to the Lord.
